A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same semantic-mapping survey. Their text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison after matching relocated content. Neither PDF contains appendices; both end with references.

before.justification: V1 synthesizes published mapping methods. Its descriptive tables and conceptual or reproduced figures report no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: V2 remains a literature survey. Its expanded method catalogues and evaluation discussion report results attributed to cited works, without original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a mapping algorithm or model. V2 expands descriptions of existing SLAM and mapping methods without introducing a procedure developed by this work.

E1.justification: Additional datasets and applications appear as characteristics of surveyed studies, particularly in v2 Tables 3–5. Neither version actually conducts training or evaluation on these datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: The expanded method tables catalogue prior research. Neither version experimentally evaluates a comparator set against a proposed method.

E3.justification: V2 Section 6 expands discussion of metrics such as OSR, nDTW and ATE, but does not apply them in experiments conducted by this work. No experimental splits, budgets or testing procedures are introduced or revised.

E4.justification: The expanded challenges and evaluation sections provide conceptual analysis of prior research. Neither version reports original ablations, sensitivity experiments, robustness tests or empirical case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests for empirical results. V2's additional discussion of entropy and uncertainty-aware mapping concerns surveyed techniques and possible evaluation measures.

E6.justification: V2 adds qualitative findings attributed to cited work, including MapNav improving VLM object grounding and InstructNav improving generic instruction following in Sections 5.1 and 5.2.2. These are secondary reports, without new numerical comparisons or original experiments.

T1.justification: V2 Section 2.2.1 adds formal SLAM motion and observation models, residuals, and weighted least-squares and pose-graph objectives in Equations 1–5. The existing projection equations are retained as Equations 6–7; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The two-axis taxonomy and emphasis on open-vocabulary, task-agnostic maps remain. V2 drops the introduction's 'first comprehensive review' assertion and replaces v1's explicit exclusion of real-world robotics with an aim to connect embodied AI and SLAM.

C2.justification: V1's brief Section 3.5 is relocated and substantially expanded into v2 Section 7, adding substantive discussion of multimodal alignment, lifelong learning and accumulated semantic errors. Section 6 also develops limitations of metric applicability, ground-truth availability and uncertainty-based evaluation.

D1.justification: V2 supplies additional technical summaries of previously cited systems, including LM-Nav's modified Dijkstra planner and RoboHop's mean aggregation in Table 6. These are documentation additions about surveyed implementations; neither version supplies an original implementation or reproduction package.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands robotics, SLAM and dense-representation literature, including ConceptFusion, NICE-SLAM and GaussianGrasper. It also explicitly distinguishes its representation-based organization from the previously cited Song et al. survey and integrates robotics methods throughout the taxonomy.

P1.justification: The introduction is rewritten, background sections are reorganized, dense geometric maps receive separate point-cloud and neural-field subsections, and evaluation is divided into intrinsic and extrinsic categories. Challenges move from Section 3.5 to an expanded Section 7, while much encoding and future-directions prose is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds dense-geometric-map Table 5 and evaluation Table 7, substantially expands existing tables, and adds a Task column to Table 4. The overview moves from Figure 4 to Figure 1 with revised labeling, and Figure 3 gains a SLAM architecture panel. Other figure artwork is retained.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies v1's conflation of point clouds and neural fields and substantially strengthens the survey's connections to SLAM, metric applicability and deployment limitations. These changes improve its conceptual coherence and critical synthesis. The gains outweigh limited new documentation problems, including conflicting Le-RNR-Map aggregation labels: mean in Table 3 and latest in Table 6.
